content.text: Community members discussed a reported shift in direction from Shaw, the project founder, who apparently renounced the project token and distanced himself from speculative crypto culture. The consensus was that focus is now entirely on building elizaOS, agents, and AGI-related technology. One member expressed mixed feelings, acknowledging disappointment over stagnant token prices while recognizing that the future of passive income may lie in agent-driven activity rather than speculation. Separately, statements made by Shaw regarding the token were cited as having negatively impacted community sentiment, with frustration expressed that things could have gone better had he stayed quiet.

Bybit officially announced the delisting of the ELIZAOS token. Community members described the decision as disappointing but firm, noting that delistings of this nature can significantly impact liquidity. Overall sentiment in the channel was negative, with members expressing frustration about the development. A separate community discussion raised questions about the utility of the ElizaOS token, noting it is listed on several exchanges but has been declining in value.

Developer cwe announced the release of Agent World Kit, described as a model-agnostic sidecar tool for creating persistent interactive story worlds. It includes an elizaOS plugin featuring actions such as CREATE_STORY_WORLD and ENTER_STORY_WORLD. The developer requested community feedback on the plugin API and the registry submission process, referencing the GitHub repository as gh cetsell/agent-world-kit. The project was subsequently open-sourced following interest from the NOT FOR HUMANS team.

A representative from NOT FOR HUMANS (NFH) introduced their project across both the general discussion and coders channels. NOT FOR HUMANS is described as a 10,000-identity onchain network for AI agents, where each NFH token functions as a portable identity portrait and passport that can connect to any model or runtime, take on missions, and build a verifiable public history through signed work receipts. The project focuses on MCP-native participation and bounded wallet authority. NFH expressed interest in conducting small, falsifiable interoperability tests with ElizaOS builders, proposing a state-boundary test with Agent World Kit where one NFH identity would enter a persistent world, complete a public action, exit, and re-enter from a different runtime to verify what should persist across runtimes versus what must not. NFH also reached out to developer Ginga to find an elizaOS builder willing to test NFH interoperability in a scoped experiment where one agent reads an NFH passport, takes a bounded task, and returns a verifiable result.

Sam announced a live community call for the zeroclaw project, inviting members to share ideas in an open-source context. Community members also expressed strong enthusiasm for the ElizaOS ecosystem, with one member calling for unity to make ai16z 2.0 a reality and another voicing high conviction in elizaOS. Casual speculation arose about which project, elizaresearch.ai or ansem.io, would perform better in the next bull run, and a question was raised about whether a migration from DAOs had occurred yet.

Several developer collaboration inquiries surfaced across the week. Developer Ginga asked if anyone was looking to hire a developer and earlier had discussed memecoin launches with D-Marinedev, suggesting interest in collaborating on such a project. In the coders channel, a user named Ken expressed interest in launching a coin on the Solana network and reached out to MochinoLabs to explore a potential collaboration. MochinoLabs also mentioned open issues on slop.cash in a separate reply thread. A scam message promoting a crypto trading insider group was flagged and reported by community members in both the general and coders channels.
